items.title: Shared prerequisite: standard-Gaussian squared norm

source.anchor: stdGaussian mean, covariance and L2 APIs
source.attribution: Mathlib contributors. ASTIS packages the finite-dimensional norm-square consequence; this wording is not a quotation.

items.statement: For a standard Gaussian Z in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, ‖Z‖² is integrable and its expectation equals the real dimension.
assumptions: Complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space.

obligations.label: Squared-norm integrability and exact dimension moment

bindings.boundary: Only the standard-Gaussian squared-norm L1 identity; no independent product law, OU update, higher moment or sampler theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: Mathlib exposes standard-Gaussian mean, covariance and L2 facts separately.
assumption_deltas.lean: ASTIS combines them with a finite orthonormal basis to return squared-norm integrability and its exact integral.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is a finite-dimensional consequence of the cited formal APIs, not a strengthened probability claim.

items.title: SPHMC Algorithm 3.1 first partial momentum refresh

source.anchor: Algorithm 3.1 lines 282–300; Lemma D.4 proof lines 2177–2180
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib expands the first refresh moment calculation; it is not the authors' original wording, complete D.7, D.8 or an endorsement.

items.statement: Adjoin a fresh standard Gaussian to the incoming phase-state law and perform Algorithm 3.1's first OU half-refresh. The refreshed state is measurable and square-integrable, and its exact second moment contains the additional Gaussian term (1−exp(−h))d.
assumptions: A probability law nu on incoming (X,Pinit), with integrable combined squared distance to (x*,0) and expectation at most M.
A nonnegative phase length h and a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel state space.
Fresh standard Gaussian momentum noise represented by nu.prod(stdGaussian E).

obligations.label: Actual independent product-law refresh and zero mixed term
Exact identity and corrected consumer budget
Repeated Algorithm 3.1 law and run-wide incoming state bound (remaining)
Actual joint Picard Gaussian array and nodes/weights (remaining)
Absorption into C kappa d L_q^18 (remaining)

bindings.boundary: One first half-refresh over an abstract incoming state law. No repeated history, derivation of the line-2179 state bound, second refresh, actual Picard Gaussian array, node/weight instantiation, numerical D.7 substitution, D.8 or paper theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: Algorithm 3.1 draws zeta0 independently of the whole incoming state.
assumption_deltas.lean: Freshness is represented by the concrete product measure nu.prod(stdGaussian E).
assumption_deltas.reason: The product construction supplies actual independence instead of assuming a zero cross moment.

assumption_deltas.source: The D.7 proof says the run-wide state estimate also controls layer-one nodes and suppresses this elementary refresh calculation.
assumption_deltas.lean: The refreshed budget is explicitly M+(1−exp(−h))*finrank(E).
assumption_deltas.reason: The Gaussian innovation adds this term. Reusing M unchanged is generally false; later universal-constant arithmetic may absorb d only after its own assumptions are present.

assumption_deltas.lean: A complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space is used.
assumption_deltas.reason: This contains the Euclidean setting and preserves the norm, Gaussian covariance and dimension calculation.

assumption_deltas.source: The source's incoming state comes from the repeated Algorithm 3.1 run and D.3/Lemma 4.16.
assumption_deltas.lean: Its probability law and M-bound are explicit premises.
assumption_deltas.reason: The history construction and run-wide estimate remain separate visible red obligations rather than being assumed complete.
